description: The compatibility corpus (D43.6): saved documents that must keep loading, and the document of the current version each must load as. Every expected document was written by hand, never produced by a migration.
rule: The paths of the corpus — file in provenance, input and expected in entries — are relative to packages/test-fixtures/src, and every one lies in compatibility/: the corpus depends on no file outside its directory. The path of in a provenance record is another kind: relative to the repository, it names the fixture outside the corpus whose bytes were copied.
Every file of compatibility/ other than this manifest is the input or the expected document of an entry, and has one record in provenance.
A file of the directory vX-Y is a saved document of schema version X.Y.
A frozen input: a file that an entry names as its input never changes once it is committed, formatting included. inputSha256 is the SHA-256 of its bytes: UTF-8, LF line endings, as committed.

An expectation: the expected document of an entry is the hand-written document of the current version that its input must load as. expectedSha256 is the SHA-256 of its bytes; expectedCompositionHash is sha256(canonicalJson(document)) (D28.7), which does not depend on white space or on the order of keys.
versions is what loading the input must report: the versions the document went through, the input's own first.
An entry of the current version is expected to load as itself: its expected file is its input file.
Entries share an expectation where what they must load as is identical, the tested order of keys included: one hand-written document serves them all.

A later schema version adds a directory of its own with the hand-written expectations for the new migration target, one document for every distinct result. Every entry is re-pointed at its expectation there: every frozen input keeps an expected result of the current version. The entries are not duplicated for the new version; it gets entries of its own, at least one, for saved documents of that version, each a frozen input of its directory. No file of an earlier directory changes or is removed.

provenance says where the bytes of a file come from. origin copy: the bytes of the named fixture file at the named commit, copied so that later work on that fixture cannot change the corpus. origin written: written by hand for the corpus in the named change.
